name: hermes_64
display_name: IBM HERMES Project Chip (14 nm PCM, Le Gallo 2023): 64 cores of 256 x 256

faithfulness.note: The chip's MVM is analog: its measured error against the exact product (gallo2022a p.4-5) is not modeled, and a deployment on the bundle runs the toolchain's exact integer value law on HERMES-64's geometry, permissions and physics. The profile declares no link or NoC row, so the activation transport between cores is unpriced by name (in the paper's measurements it ran off chip through the test board's FPGA, p.5).

notes: allow_coalescing is true: "In the current design, the links can transfer data across the LDPUs of multiple cores to realize fully on-chip intra-layer partial sum accumulation, and transfer data from the LDPU to the input of a GDPU." (gallo2022a, Section II, p.3). allow_neuron_splitting is true: "The mapping of weights onto the chip is done by converting a weight matrix for each layer into 256x256 conductance sub-matrices, one for each core the layer is mapped onto. The weight matrix is split into the smallest possible amount of sub-matrices which have the same number of rows and columns, both less than 256." (gallo2022a, Methods, p.9): a layer's rows (partial sums) and its output columns span several cores. The chip's inputs are 8-bit time-encoded (Extended Data Table I, p.24); the bundle binds no activation_bits, so a run that holds the chip's input width declares activation_bits 8.
